articles.headline: Kittle and Landry Deliver on Equal Starting Volume
articles.analysis: Jarvis Landry and George Kittle supplied Kuhl with 118.40 points across eight player-starts, compared with Kyle Pitts' 63.00 across eight for Tony. Kuhl averaged 14.80 against 7.88. The narrower matched positional research reinforces the difference, 80.75 to 15.21 above benchmark, with six recorded starts on each side in that window.
articles.verdict: Kuhl has the stronger production case on equal starting volume. Keeper implications and actual lineup improvement remain unverified.

articles.headline: Gibson's Raw Edge Meets Cooper's Positional Countercase
articles.analysis: Antonio Gibson gave Stew 78.30 points across seven starts, while Amari Cooper delivered 72.50 across seven for Thommy. Stew's 5.80-point advantage is modest. In the narrower matched positional window, Cooper actually led 32.25 to 31.40 above benchmark, despite one fewer start.
articles.verdict: The exchange is closely contested on available measures. A decisive winner would overstate the evidence.

articles.headline: Lamb Delivers the Return Hunt Could Not
articles.analysis: CeeDee Lamb returned 89.20 points across eight starts for Tony. Kareem Hunt supplied Stilly with 2.80 in one. The narrower matched positional research records Lamb at 48.57 above benchmark and Hunt at minus 2.03. Stilly received little direct starting production, and the one recorded appearance fell below that research benchmark.
articles.verdict: Tony has a compelling production advantage. Verify why Hunt's ownership and starting spell ended and whether any other value was recovered before issuing a final grade.

articles.headline: Fournette Gives Stover a Clear Direct Production Edge
articles.analysis: Leonard Fournette supplied Stover with 164.80 points across nine starts, averaging 18.31. DeVonta Smith returned 69.10 across eight for Kuhl, averaging 8.64. The narrower positional research matches Smith at 20.54 above benchmark but does not resolve Fournette, who also appears in Kuhl's earlier documented exchange with Evans.
articles.verdict: Stover has the stronger raw production case. Reconstruct Fournette's ownership spells and resolve his positional evidence before evaluating both sides.

articles.headline: Mixon Outproduces Koble's Two-Back Return
articles.analysis: Joe Mixon supplied Tony with 193.10 points in ten starts. Zack Moss and James Robinson contributed 137.60 across fifteen for Koble. Tony averaged 19.31 per start against 9.17, extracting more total points in fewer appearances. The narrower positional research records Mixon at 114.44 above benchmark but leaves Koble's package unmatched.
articles.verdict: Tony leads both raw measures by a meaningful margin. Koble's missing positional and ownership evidence prevents a definitive grade.

articles.headline: Dillon's Return Survives in an Incomplete Trade Record
articles.analysis: AJ Dillon supplied Stilly with 54.40 points across five starts, averaging 10.88. The narrower research records 22.62 points above benchmark across three starts. The archived receipt does not identify the other participant or what Stilly surrendered.
articles.verdict: The surviving record establishes a documented return, not the quality of the exchange. Recover the missing side before assigning a winner or grade.

articles.headline: Evans Leads on Volume in a Nearly Identical Efficiency Contest
articles.analysis: Aaron Rodgers and Keenan Allen generated 391.50 points across twenty-two player-starts for Evans. Leonard Fournette, Patrick Mahomes and Brandon Aiyuk delivered 231.40 across thirteen for Kuhl. Both packages averaged 17.80 per start when rounded to two decimals. The narrower positional research matches part of Kuhl's return but none of Evans' package. Fournette subsequently appears in another documented exchange involving Kuhl.
articles.verdict: Evans has the greater recorded volume, but the nearly identical efficiency and incomplete positional evidence complicate an overall judgment.

articles.headline: Stew's Backfield Package Holds a Modest Edge
articles.analysis: Kenyan Drake and Saquon Barkley delivered 100.40 points across nine player-starts for Stew. Nyheim Miller-Hines, Clyde Edwards-Helaire and Ty'Son Williams supplied Kuhl with 84.40 across eight. Stew averaged 11.16 against 10.55. The partial positional research favors Stew, 49.13 to 28.90 above benchmark, but each package contains an unmatched asset.
articles.verdict: Stew leads the recorded production measures by a modest margin. Both sides require complete positional and ownership evidence before grading.

articles.headline: Birch's Three-Player Package Builds a Substantial Return
articles.analysis: Lamar Jackson, Mark Andrews and Josh Jacobs supplied Birch with 577.58 points across thirty-six player-starts. Dak Prescott, Noah Fant and Antonio Gibson returned 364.60 across twenty-six for Thommy. Birch led in both volume and efficiency, 16.04 to 14.02 per start. The narrower matched positional research likewise favors Birch, 263.54 to 131.75 above benchmark. Jacobs appears in Thommy's acquisition the previous day.
articles.verdict: Birch has a strong documented direct-production case. Thommy's substantial return and the connected transactions deserve independent evaluation.

articles.headline: Tony's Opening-Week Package Outproduces Thommy's Return
articles.analysis: Corey Davis, A.J. Brown and Jonathan Taylor delivered 414.50 points across twenty-five player-starts for Tony. Tyreek Hill, Josh Jacobs and Javonte Williams supplied Thommy with 333.10 across twenty-four. Tony averaged 16.58 against 13.88. The narrower positional research favors Tony's matched package, 262.49 to 190.47 above benchmark, but Jacobs is unmatched and appears in Thommy's next documented trade the following day.
articles.verdict: Tony has the stronger recorded direct return. Thommy's rapid subsequent use of Jacobs must be reconciled before assessing the original exchange.
